what: A still frame's time at the worst 1835 stand, per Scene detail tier and release viewport, held as a ceiling beside T-1975's triangle ceilings (DETAIL in renderers/web/js/main.js). Gated by `node tools/measure_still_frame.mjs --gate`; .github/workflows/chicago-4d-frame-time.yml runs it.
unit: screens: the frame's time over a bare screen's (every layer hidden: clear and sky, one call) timed in the same page at the same pixel ratio. Headless Chromium rasterises in software (SwiftShader), so a millisecond is the runner's and not the scene's; a faster or slower runner moves both in step, and only the ratio is gated. The milliseconds are printed beside it and recorded below.
rule: the reading at the worst stand plus 10 %, rounded up to 5 screens. A parcel that makes every frame slower argues its own number here, with its reading, in the same commit; a parcel that makes frames cheaper brings the number down to its reading by the same rule.
stand_why: T-2084's back yard on Washington and Wells: the worst 1835 stand at every tier and both viewports in T-2099's table (docs/measurements/T-2099-still-frame.md). 1904's landing is slower still and is T-2109's to fix; this holds 1835.

measured.on: 2026-10-04, dev @ 29fa96f2, published mirror, steward runner (4 cores), ANGLE SwiftShader; desktop 1280x800 dpr 1; phone 390x780 dpr 3, Image sharpness Medium (1.5), CPU 4x throttled; medians of 2 frames, bare screen of 5
